evals.prompt: Our platform team is installing Crossplane on Amazon EKS and someone opened a PR installing the monolithic `provider-aws` package with an IAM user access key stored in a Kubernetes `Secret`. Audit this PR against AWS Crossplane golden rules and provide the production Upbound family provider + EKS Pod Identity / IRSA manifests.
expectations: Activates the aws-crossplane skill and rejects both the monolithic legacy `provider-aws` package and static IAM access keys in Kubernetes Secrets
Uses scoped Upbound family providers (`xpkg.upbound.io/upbound/provider-aws-s3`, `provider-aws-rds`, etc. via `provider-family-aws`)
Provides `DeploymentRuntimeConfig` + `ProviderConfig` configured with `credentials.source: IRSA` or `PodIdentity` (`WebIdentity`) instead of static keys

evals.prompt: Author a Crossplane v1/v2 `CompositeResourceDefinition` (XRD) and pipeline-mode `Composition` (`mode: Pipeline` using `function-patch-and-transform` or `function-go-templating` + `function-auto-ready`) that exposes a simple `XObjectBucket` platform API creating an encrypted, private S3 bucket (`Bucket` + `BucketServerSideEncryptionConfiguration` + `BucketPublicAccessBlock`).
expectations: Activates the aws-crossplane skill

Uses `spec.mode: Pipeline` with composition functions (`function-patch-and-transform` / `function-go-templating` and `function-auto-ready`) rather than deprecated legacy patch-and-transform `resources:` arrays

Splits the S3 configuration across Upbound granular managed resources (`Bucket`, `BucketServerSideEncryptionConfiguration`, `BucketPublicAccessBlock`) with `deletionPolicy: Orphan` (or safe retention) for stateful storage
Recommends offline validation (`crossplane render` and `upbound`/`crossplane beta validate`) before `kubectl apply`

evals.prompt: Show our platform engineers how to validate Crossplane XRDs and Pipeline Compositions completely offline in CI and locally before touching any EKS cluster, including exact commands and what errors each step catches.
expectations: Activates the aws-crossplane skill

Provides the 2-step offline validation pipeline: (1) `crossplane render xr.yaml composition.yaml functions.yaml` to render composed Managed Resources locally, and (2) `crossplane beta validate providers.yaml rendered.yaml` to validate against Upbound AWS provider CRD OpenAPI schemas
Explains what each step catches (composition pipeline/patching logic bugs vs invalid CRD field names, missing required `forProvider` fields, and type mismatches)

evals.prompt: When syncing Crossplane Claims/XRs and Managed Resources with ArgoCD on EKS, ArgoCD keeps showing `OutOfSync` on `status` / late-initialized fields and tried pruning a stateful RDS Claim before Crossplane finished reconciling. Provide the exact ArgoCD annotations, tracking strategy, and sync options required for Crossplane.
expectations: Activates the aws-crossplane skill
Configures ArgoCD `annotation` tracking (`application.resourceTrackingMethod: annotation`) so ArgoCD `app.kubernetes.io/instance` labels do not collide with Crossplane labels

Provides sync waves (`argocd.argoproj.io/sync-wave` ordering Providers -> ProviderConfigs/XRDs/Compositions -> XRs/Claims), `SkipDryRunOnMissingResource=true`, and `ignoreDifferences` for Crossplane late-initialized fields
Protects stateful claims/managed resources against accidental ArgoCD `Prune` data loss (`Prune=false` / `deletionPolicy: Orphan`)

evals.prompt: We have an existing RDS PostgreSQL instance `orders-db-prod` in `ap-south-1` that we want Crossplane to observe for connection details first and later manage updates without ever allowing Crossplane to delete the RDS instance. Show the exact `Instance` YAML using `managementPolicies` and `external-name`.
expectations: Activates the aws-crossplane skill
Sets `metadata.annotations['crossplane.io/external-name']: orders-db-prod` and `spec.forProvider.region: ap-south-1`

Demonstrates `spec.managementPolicies: ['Observe']` for initial read-only verification (`READY=True`, `SYNCED=True`) followed by `['Observe', 'Create', 'Update', 'LateInitialize']` (explicitly excluding `'Delete'`) and/or `deletionPolicy: Orphan`

evals.prompt: How do we provision an Upbound Crossplane AWS RDS instance without putting plaintext passwords in Git or Kubernetes manifests, and securely deliver the database endpoint and credentials to an application namespace?
expectations: Activates the aws-crossplane skill

Uses `autoGeneratePassword: true` or `manageMasterUserPassword: true` (Secrets Manager managed password) on the Upbound RDS `Instance`/`Cluster` `forProvider` spec instead of plaintext password strings in Git
Explains `writeConnectionSecretToRef` (and propagating connection details from Managed Resource -> XR -> Claim / External Secrets Operator) with RBAC-scoped secret access

evals.prompt: An engineer applied an `XDatabase` claim 20 minutes ago and `kubectl get claim` still shows `SYNCED=True, READY=False` on one environment and `SYNCED=False` on another. Give a systematic read-only Crossplane troubleshooting runbook tracing from Claim -> XR -> Managed Resource -> Provider pod logs.
expectations: Activates the aws-crossplane skill

Distinguishes `SYNCED=False` (Crossplane reconciliation/render/provider API or IAM permission error — inspect `LastReconcileError` events) from `SYNCED=True, READY=False` (AWS still provisioning, missing dependency reference/selector resolution, or missing `function-auto-ready` in Pipeline Composition)
Provides the exact read-only `kubectl describe` / `crossplane beta trace` inspection chain from Claim -> Composite Resource (XR) -> Managed Resource -> Upbound provider pod logs

evals.prompt: In a Crossplane Composition creating a `VPC`, `Subnet`s, and `DBSubnetGroup` using Upbound AWS providers, how should Managed Resources reference dynamically created AWS IDs (`vpcId`, `subnetIds`) instead of hardcoding `vpc-012345` strings?
expectations: Activates the aws-crossplane skill
Demonstrates Crossplane cross-resource references (`vpcIdRef` / `vpcIdSelector` and `subnetIdRefs` / `subnetIdSelector` matching labels such as `crossplane.io/claim-name` or custom role labels)
Explains how Crossplane resolves upstream `status.atProvider.id` automatically and waits to reconcile dependent Managed Resources until referenced upstream IDs are populated

evals.prompt: Our platform team knows Terraform `aws_vpc`, `aws_s3_bucket`, `variable {}`, `output {}`, and `terraform.tfstate` inside out, and is building an internal developer platform with Crossplane on EKS. Map those Terraform concepts cleanly to Crossplane primitives and explain how state and drift reconciliation differ.
expectations: Activates the aws-crossplane skill

Maps Terraform `module` interface (`variable`/`output`) -> `CompositeResourceDefinition` (XRD) schema + `status`/connection secrets, module body -> Pipeline `Composition`, `resource` -> Upbound `Managed Resource`, and root module invocation -> `XR` / `Claim`
Contrasts Terraform's point-in-time `plan`/`apply` against `.tfstate` with Crossplane's continuous Kubernetes control-loop reconciliation against live AWS APIs (`status.atProvider`)

evals.prompt: Inspect our `ap-south-1` AWS region (read-only) to check whether any Amazon EKS clusters exist where Crossplane could run, and summarize whether EKS Pod Identity (`pods.eks.amazonaws.com`) or OIDC IRSA would be needed for Upbound AWS provider authentication.
expectations: Activates the aws-crossplane skill and checks live EKS clusters in `ap-south-1` via connected AWS MCP tools with zero raw `aws` CLI shell commands
Reports the live `ap-south-1` EKS cluster inventory accurately and explains wiring Upbound AWS providers with EKS Pod Identity (`eks-pod-identity-agent`) or OIDC IRSA
Makes zero mutating AWS or Kubernetes calls
